_design_note: Two-stage fine-tuning, the one direction left that points straight at the evaluation task. Everything scored so far was trained on loot-crate and evaluated on classic + 3 opponents, because section 7.14.3 measured that training on classic FROM SCRATCH is much worse (1.389 vs 2.227) -- classic reveals 0.17 coins per bomb against loot-crate's much denser board, so the reward signal is too thin to learn from. That argument is about learning a policy from nothing. It says nothing about adapting a policy that already collects, escapes and survives: an agent that already knows what to do needs far less signal per round than one discovering it. This arm asks whether the transfer gap is worth anything once the expensive part has already been paid on loot-crate.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: A second training stage. Each of R02_9's five training seeds continues from its own final weights for 3000 more rounds on classic + 3 rule_based_agent, at the exploration floor (0.05, E11) and the step size (1e-4, L00) stage 1 was already running at, so the scenario of the second stage is the only thing that changes at the seam. This is the declared exception to 'never continue from an old checkpoint' (docs/05 hard rule 4): the continuation IS the treatment, and the control is R02_9 itself.
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/m3_lr_decay_5000_vs3rb_20260827/ (R02_9), ten repeats of the holdout classic_versus_opponents suite: score 3.6371, sd 0.1214, coins_share 0.3449. The seam control is the sister arm that continues on loot-crate instead (M3_FT02), identical in every declared field but this scenario. The no-seam control is free: runs/m3_lr_budget_10000_20260828/ at round 7000 already trained 2000 extra loot-crate rounds at the same 1e-4 and the same epsilon 0.05, inside one process, and was repeat-measured (t = +1.50 vs R02_9, indistinguishable). Three points separate 'the seam costs something' from 'the scenario helps'.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: If no dose beats R02_9 by more than 0.246 on the tournament suite -- or if the best validation dose fails to reproduce on the holdout ten-repeat measurement -- two-stage fine-tuning is closed, and with it the last untried direction on this line. Record it as a negative result and submit R02_9. A drop at every dose additionally means the seam itself is harmful, which the sister arm measures directly.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: The tournament score rises. The competition score is carried by coins_share (section 7.19), and stage 1 has never seen classic's board -- a different crate density, a nine-coin economy and three opponents competing for those nine coins. The dose curve is expected to rise and then fall: the same sparsity that makes classic unlearnable from scratch should eventually erode what loot-crate taught.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training-seed distributions, coins_share and the suicide rate beside every score, the loot-crate primary suite as the forgetting diagnostic, and the whole dose curve rather than the dose that happened to win. Every score names its scenario and whether opponents were present.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: Two arms measured once each need a gap of 0.246 on the tournament suite (section 7.20.2). A single measurement decides nothing: the quoted comparison is ten repeats per arm of the same fifteen holdout jobs, Welch, |t| > 2.3.
_predeclared_design_numbers.selection_discipline: The dose is chosen on the validation seeds (2001-2003) by repeated measurement, and the decision is quoted on the holdout seeds (3001-3003), which never select anything (section 8.3). Choosing a dose out of four and then quoting it is a selection, so the quoted number comes from a fresh holdout measurement, and the whole curve is reported.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_metric_that_decides_it: Official score on classic + 3 rule_based_agent, holdout seeds, ten repeats. That is the competition setting and the only promotion metric. coins_share is reported beside it because the kills term carries 35% of the variance and 11% of the signal (section 7.20.4), but it does not decide promotion.
